rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The chapter asks whether a cleric obtains a desirable appointment.
rules.original_conditions_and_uncertainty: Separate from Chapter LXXV before the divider.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Outcome is church appointment rather than demonstrated moral worth.
The opening attacks perceived clergy greed.
Lilly says the same question applies across denominations.
The first-house ruler signifies the applicant.
Moon supplies a second applicant significator.
The ninth lord signifies the desired church living.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: first Lord or Moon joined ninth Lord
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: A connection between applicant and ninth ruler is favorable.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: ninth Lord in ninth or beholds it
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Ninth ruler in or aspecting its house is positive.
Lilly forecasts appointment.
rules.original_conditions_and_uncertainty: No independently documented recipient or decision.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Successful appointment may require substantial effort.
An applicant significator in ninth may be favorable.
Source lists conditions reversing favorable reading.
rules.original_conditions_and_uncertainty: Do not treat ninth placement as sufficient.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Adverse square without reception portends trouble.
Lilly proposes an appointment failing after seeming close.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: ninth Lord in first or applies applicant
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Alternative favorable disposition of ninth ruler to applicant.
The author expects easier appointment.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: first Lord trine sextile Sun Jupiter
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Specific favorable aspects with Sun or Jupiter are cited.
The favorable planet is assumed in rising house.
The combination allegedly secures promotion.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: first ninth Lord sextile or trine Reception
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Beneficial first–ninth lord aspect with reception is favorable.
Lilly says the position may be obtained without a payment.
Hard square with reception is a separate outcome branch.
rules.original_conditions_and_uncertainty: Do not collapse square with sextile.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: eventually obtained with contribution to Patron
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He expects eventual success after difficulty or financial consideration.
rules.original_conditions_and_uncertainty: The author mentions possible payment; not an independent bribery case.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: planet transfers ninth Lord light to first
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: A mediating planet carries influence between ninth lord and applicant.
The author conjectures a third person may obtain the appointment.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: heavier planet carries translator virtue elsewhere
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: A subsequent transfer to another planet can overturn that reading.
He allows a near-complete proceeding to collapse after subsequent contact.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: first Lord applies ninth without obstructive aspect
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Direct application without other adverse intervention favors success.
rules.original_conditions_and_uncertainty: Absence of adverse interim aspect required.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The author expects success but with effort or petitioning.
Multiple planets may represent additional applicants.
rules.original_conditions_and_uncertainty: Alternative: many difficulties rather than competitors.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The process may involve prolonged dispute or work.
rules.original_conditions_and_uncertainty: Not the same endpoint as losing appointment.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Lord first conjunct Infortune no reception
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: A contact to malefic not ruling ninth and lacking reception is adverse.
Lilly predicts failure under adverse conditions.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Infortune commits virtue to strong Fortune
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Transfer from adverse planet to strong benefic is said to rescue outcome.
An initially unfavorable matter becomes successful under the exception.
Malefic conjunction without reception is framed as unproductive.
Reception changes the same adverse configuration to success with difficulty.
The effecting planet in angle allegedly hastens appointment.
A succedent position delays the matter.
A cadent effecting planet is claimed to destroy prospect.
rules.original_conditions_and_uncertainty: Do not collapse cadent and succedent.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly admits a rare unexpected success even when other testimonies fail.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: malevolent aspects first Lord or Moon square opposition no Reception
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Unfavorable square/opposition absent reception is an additional source condition.
rules.original_conditions_and_uncertainty: Actor and aspect must be kept.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The author conjectures dissatisfaction with proceedings.
He attributes suspicion of negligent or corrupt intermediaries.
rules.original_conditions_and_uncertainty: A reported belief, not proof that real agents were corrupt.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: first and ninth Lords commit disposition to another Planet
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Both source significators transfer influence to one planet.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: receiving planet not impedited Retrograde before sign exit
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Freedom from obstruction or retrograde reversal is a qualifier.
rules.original_conditions_and_uncertainty: Grammar across page seam must be retained.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly interprets the combination as success.
A dignified Moon is linked to outside support.
The author expects allies or supporters.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: ninth Lord joined fourth Lord or reverse
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Ninth/fourth lord contact in either direction is an additional favorable rule.
Appointment is expected with comparatively little effort.
The author separately asks whether the appointment is valuable.
The tenth and its ruler/occupants are used to assess the position value.
rules.original_conditions_and_uncertainty: Ninth represents award; tenth value is different.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Dignified angular planets are positive testimony.
The author forecasts a lucrative living.
rules.original_conditions_and_uncertainty: No salary, property or independent appointment documents.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly criticizes opponents of astrology among clergy.
rules.original_conditions_and_uncertainty: Seventeenth-century polemical perspective, not universal fact.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly denies encouraging corrupt purchase of church positions.
rules.original_conditions_and_uncertainty: Authorial self-claim, not independent verification of conduct.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The author insults another critic of astrology.
rules.original_conditions_and_uncertainty: Keep attribution and historical language separate from evidence.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Closing text is argumentative rather than a worked predictive case.
rules.original_conditions_and_uncertainty: Do not add empirical case success.
